notes: Photos are no longer all vertical. Every engine had portrait hard-wired into it — fal was pinned to portrait_4_3, the RunPod workflow to 832×1216, and GLM to its two portrait sizes — so a wide balcony view, a room, or two people side by side came back as a tall crop of itself. The photo director now chooses the orientation per shot: portrait for selfies and standing figures, landscape for wide scenes and people side by side, square for overhead flat-lays and tight details. Each engine maps the choice to its own sizes (fal's landscape_4_3 and square_hd, 1216×832 and 1024×1024 on the GPU, GLM's equivalents), selfies through Kontext keep following the reference photo's shape, and the director's choice is printed in both its own log line and the route line — an unstated or invalid answer falls back to portrait, so nothing breaks when the model shrugs.
